- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–3 days); cap forecast rise at +3% after spike, unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral/bearish, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply downward correction of 1–2% for final 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or fading.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days to account for lag.
